Hi Laura,

Specifically:

- Is billing prorated (per-token) or rounded up to 1k-token blocks?
- Any examples showing invoice impact for a typical exchange (example below): prompt ~200 tokens, model returns ~400 tokens; 10k calls/month.

If you have the Q2 rate card PDF, please attach. We're putting together a one-page budget to show to procurement.

Hi Marta — great to hear from you. Attaching the Q2 rate card and a short mapping below to help procurement. I kept the math simple and included both per-request and monthly roll-up examples for the 200/400 token exchange you mentioned. Notes at the bottom on rounding and fallback behavior.

Summary (high-level):
- Chat endpoint (chat/completions API): billable units = prompt tokens + response tokens (the whole conversation chunk for that request). Rate used in example: $0.06 per 1,000 tokens.
- Responses endpoint: billable units = prompt tokens + response tokens (same counting approach) but priced slightly lower due to simplified I/O and model packaging; example rate: $0.045 per 1,000 tokens.
- Legacy completions: historically we billed primarily on output tokens for single-turn completions. In this example we treat legacy as output-only billing at $0.05 per 1,000 output tokens.

Example math (single exchange: prompt 200 tokens, response 400 tokens = 600 total tokens):
- Chat endpoint: 600 tokens * ($0.06 / 1000) = $0.036 per call. For 10,000 calls/month = $360.
- Responses endpoint: 600 tokens * ($0.045 / 1000) = $0.027 per call. For 10,000 calls/month = $270.
- Legacy completions (output-only): 400 tokens * ($0.05 / 1000) = $0.02 per call. For 10,000 calls/month = $200.

Rounding and invoicing rules (hosted API):
- We bill proportionally per 1,000 tokens (i.e., you are charged a fractional amount; we do not round every request up to a full 1k block). Example above is prorated.
- Token counting: chat and responses count input+output. Legacy completions count output only (single-turn).
- Model fallback: if we route a request to a fallback model (policy-based), billing uses the model variant actually served. We include model name in logs so you can reconcile.

Quick notes on commitment/discounts:
- The hosted API has no hard minimum monthly invoice, but we offer committed pricing/credits for customers that want predictable budgeting (applies to Dedicated translations and large hosted commitments).

I've attached the rate card. If you want, I can produce this same table as a 1-page PDF with your expected call volumes and your preferred model class plugged in (gives procurement a line item they can drop into a PO).

Best,

Thanks, Laura — this is exactly what we needed. Two quick follow-ups before I share with procurement:

1) When you say "bill proportionally" — do you aggregate tokens at the account level per billing period or at the individual request level before prorating? If we have lots of micro-requests, I want to confirm there's no unexpected rounding behavior.
2) If a request falls back to a cheaper model variant due to capacity, do you automatically credit the difference or simply bill what's served (and surface the fallback in logs)? Procurement is sensitive to surprises here.

Also — any chance you can show the same 10k-call example assuming a 15% introductory discount for the first 6 months? That's what the budget owner asked for to gauge runway.

Thanks,
Marta

Karthik — forwarding Finera's follow-ups. Procurement asked for two clarifications (aggregation/rounding + fallback crediting) and a pro-forma with a 15% intro discount for 6 months. I drafted the short answers below; please correct any finance/legal bits before I send back to Marta. Also thinking we can offer a 15% discount on hosted usage for first 6 months (no change to tiering or rate card PDF) and capture in HubSpot deal RDW-2345.

Draft responses for Finera:
- Aggregation: tokens are totaled per account across the billing period and invoiced prorated (we do not round up per-request to the next 1k). This avoids per-request rounding inflation for high-volume micro-calls.
- Fallbacks: we bill the model actually used. We do not proactively credit differences when automatic fallback happens; instead, fallbacks are surfaced in our logs and console. For large customers we can include a fallback-reporting clause and an SLA credit mechanism if you want that formalized.
- 15% intro discount example (6 months): using the numbers Laura sent — Responses endpoint estimate (baseline $270/month for 10k calls) => with 15% discount = $229.50/month. I'll attach a one-page with month-by-month totals if you want to push this to procurement.

If finance/legal are OK, I'll send answers and the discounted pro-forma back to Marta today. HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/2345

Thanks,
Laura
